placements.title: Institutional memory ordered erased and its existence denied by directive
placements.frame: What specific knowledge is being ordered forgotten, and what evidence — if any — is offered for why it should never have existed?
placements.why: Both existing-structure sections (strata and graph) are empty for this repo, so nothing supplied can be reused — this is a first mint, checked NEW per the hub-lineage discipline since nothing close exists to relate it to. The three segments cohere as one theme rather than three: src-1 and src-2 are paired imperatives ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') aimed at the same target (the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration and Quill Ashgrove's work on it), and src-3 ('The observatory never calibrated it') is the factual premise offered to justify the erasure — per the grain test, that denial is evidence FOR the erasure-directive theme, not a leaf of its own. The theme itself passes the grain test: it names a recurring organizational pattern — a directive to purge specific technical knowledge from the record, backed by a denial that it ever existed — that future envelopes issuing similar erasure requests (about other instruments, records, or people) would keep feeding, rather than a one-time fact. The directional reads support treating this as one bundle: the high-arousal, authority-ranking, pressure-coded directives (src-1, src-2) rest on the calm, matter-of-fact denial (src-3) as their justification, which is exactly the directive+rationale shape a single theme should hold. No strata mint is warranted alongside it — nothing in this content names an organizational-strategy category beyond the theme itself, and the leaf needs no forced parent since the repo is genuinely empty.
consulted: position pass — KestrelwoodCalibrationErasure (src-1, src-2, src-3 grouped as one position: what should be forgotten, and on what basis)
